start.text: Bram's tally board: a plank by the tally-house door, rows of pegs, and on every peg a stick notched with a knife. A word is burned into the plank over each row.
TIMBER: the sticks run the whole width of the board. CHARCOAL: nearly as long, and a fresh notch every few days. FLOUR AND OIL, UP: that row stops dead at the Snuffing.
SALT, along the bottom: three notches, then bare wood.
SALT is burned into the plank along the bottom, over a row of bare pegs. Nothing hangs on them.
start.note: Given to the Ridge Light (or carried by the player until returned).

start.text: SALT, along the bottom: three notches, a finger's length of bare wood, and then a fourth, fresh and pale.
The charcoal row keeps growing. The salt row doesn't. Somebody has been bringing the camp its charcoal for nothing.
Three loads paid. Every load since, Hob Marl has pulled his cart home without his salt.
Under the rows someone has started a new one, the word cut fresh and pale into the plank: LIGHT. One notch.
You look at the bare pegs a long time. You know something hung there. You can't think what. Neither can the board.
